title: Generic groundwater application orchestration — production FMR cross-language application context
goal: Materialize the narrow production cross-language application context that exposes admitted F-GC49A plan authority and F-GC49B participant handles to the admitted F-GC49C generic Python service without transferring SWAP state, F-GC40/F-GC33 mathematics, ledger ownership or predictor/corrector ownership into Python.
design: Fortran application context binds externally owned application plan, participant registry, participant handles and ledgers.
Context validates tile-handle and tile-ledger identity against the admitted plan and topology.
Corrector routing and aggregation remain Fortran-owned and delegate aggregation to F-GC40.
Linear-response evaluation and reanchoring remain in the F-GC33 authority; Stage D calls that authority rather than reproducing formulas in Python.
Opaque cross-language context handles reference Fortran-owned contexts; Python receives only immutable primitive views and operation results.
Python adapter implements the existing GroundwaterApplicationRuntime protocol by calling the C ABI; it never owns participant state, candidate state or ledger state.
Publication ordering remains F-GC49C/F-GC41: MODFLOW publication first, then SWAP commits, then ledger commits.
exclusions: Python F-GC33 HCOF/RHS evaluation or reanchoring
next_permitted_action: F-GC49 is closed through Stage D. No further F-GC49 expansion is authorized by this workunit. Any broader iMOD Coupler product integration, physics-envelope expansion, or heterogeneous N:1 transferability work requires a separately bounded capability; SCALE remains a separate scientific line.

reconcile_findings: Canonical contains F-GC49A plan authority and F-GC49B participant registry as production Fortran capabilities, but no generic cross-language FMR application ABI.
src/adapter/mod_modflow6_fgc34_c_bridge.f90 is a production MODFLOW package publisher only and does not expose FMR participants.

tests/fgc/support/mod_fgc44_real_swap_c_bridge.f90 through mod_fgc47_mixed_topology_c_bridge.f90 are qualification fixtures; they own fixture SWAP state/physics/ledgers and are explicitly ineligible for promotion.

The admitted F-GC49C Python runtime protocol already defines the required operation boundary: plan, origin capture, cell flux evaluation, corrector trials, discard, reanchoring, preflight, ledger preparation and publication.

Stage D therefore requires a Fortran-owned application context over externally owned F-GC49A plan, F-GC49B registry/handles and ledgers, plus a narrow opaque-handle C ABI and a Python adapter. The C ABI may expose primitive immutable views but must not own SWAP state or reproduce cell/linear-response mathematics.
